svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.25.4.2 Vapour Barrier Materials
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.25 HEAT TRANSFER, AIR LEAKAGE AND CONDENSATION CONTROL
Vapour Barrier Materials

g.text: barrier, dry cup 60 or less, wet cup more than 300, (2)
Foamed plastic as the vapour barrier: thick

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as provided in Sentence (2), vapour barriers have a permeance not
greater than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m²) (1.05 US perms) measured in accordance with
ASTM E96/E96M, "Standard Test Methods for Water Vapor Transmission of
Materials" using the desiccant method (dry cup).
Thermally insulated foundation wall assemblies are permitted to be
constructed with variable-permeance vapour barriers having a permeance
not greater than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m²) (1.05 US perms) using the desiccant
method (dry cup) and greater than 300 ng/(Pa×s×m²) (5.24 US perms) using
the water method (wet cup) measured in accordance with ASTM E96/E96M,
"Standard Test Methods for Water Vapor Transmission of Materials." (See
Where the intended use of the interior space will result in high moisture
generation, the assembly is designed according to Part 5. (See Note
Where polyethylene is installed to serve only as the vapour barrier, it
complies with Clause 4.4, Thermal Stability, and Clause 5.7, Oxidative
Induction Time, of CAN/CGSB-51.34-M, "Vapour Barrier, Polyethylene Sheet
for Use in Building Construction."
Membrane-type vapour barriers other than polyethylene conform to the
requirements of CAN/CGSB-51.33-M, "Vapour Barrier Sheet, Excluding
Polyethylene, for Use in Building Construction."
Membrane-type vapour barriers other than polyethylene that are
susceptible to deterioration under prolonged exposure to direct
ultraviolet radiation
(a) are covered, or (b) are only installed in locations that are not exposed to
direct ultraviolet radiation after the completion of construction. (See Note
Where a coating is applied to gypsum board to function as the vapour
barrier, the permeance of the coating is determined in accordance with
CAN/CGSB-1.501-M, "Method for Permeance of Coated Wallboard."
Where foamed plastic insulation functions as the vapour barrier, it is
sufficiently thick so as to meet the requirement of Sentence (1).
Drawn: test dishes cut in half, purple dashed arrows are water vapour. US perms converted at 1 perm = 57.2135 ng/(Pa×s×m²). Thicknesses are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.25.4.2. (page 9-236)
